articles.title: North Sea, Nature Untamed review – stunning footage finds the beauty and splendour under the water
articles.summary: Diver Peter van Rodijnen’s footage of basking whales, plankton blooms and fatherly fish disputes the idea that the North Sea is a bleak wilderness. The North Sea, with its cold grey waters, is the world’s drabbest.
body: First, the greyness. Van Rodijnen films the North Sea’s waves sparkling with the cosmic blue light of bioluminescent algae, and lit up with the disco colours of coral and plankton blooms. He also brings us cute, coo-worthy stories from the depths; take the male shorthorn sculpin fish (no looker, it must be said) who spends the winter looking after his eggs, cleaning and blowing fresh water over them. Van Rodijnen’s camera is there for the baby fish hatching – pop, pop, pop out of their pearly plump pink eggs. There are some quirky stories, too, including a barnacle with a superlong penis.

articles.title: Remake review – Ross McElwee’s magnificent and moving tribute to a tragic loss and the art it inspired
articles.summary: Sherman’s March director McElwee revisits footage of his late son for this magnificently affecting film and meditation on making art. This new film from revered documentary-maker Ross McElwee is an extraordinary work, arguably his most audacious use yet of autobiographical material while at the…
body: On that very simplest level, Remake starts out as a documentation of how Hollywood got in touch with McElwee and told him they wanted to make a fictionalised remake of his best-known film, Sherman’s March. Made in 1985 with a one-man crew (McElwee himself), Sherman’s March recorded the McElwee’s trip back to South Carolina where he grew up; there he films his family, old friends, and himself as he continually fails to establish romantic relationships with various women, all of it lavishly slathered with his own warm, softly southern-accented voiceover.

Remake slowly reveals what it was that led to Adrian’s death – not in order to create any kind of salacious mystery, but because it only makes sense, as much as something so senseless ever will, after we’ve got to know Adrian better: his aspirations and his troubles, a bipolar diagnosis, the deep wells of self-doubt that are not unlike his father’s. The end result is a profoundly moving work, one that will resonate with anyone who is a parent or close to a troubled kid, but one that has so much more about the making of art, its joys and its dishonesties. It lingers in the mind long after the tears have dried.

articles.title: MIP London Ending After Two Years as Organizers Launch New Event at London Book Fair
articles.summary: MIP London will not be returning in 2027, with organizers RX France instead launching a new event alongside the London Book Fair. Titled MIP Talks, the two-day conference will take place March 16-17, 2027 — concurrent to the book fair — with the aim of “bringing together leading voices from across…
body: “The boundaries of entertainment have all but disappeared,” said Lucy Smith, director of the entertainment division at RX France, in a statement. “IP can come from anywhere, audiences don’t think in sectors and an idea can travel further and faster than ever before. MIP has always been about understanding where the entertainment business is going next. MIP Talks at the London Book Fair takes that curiosity further bringing together the people shaping what breaks through, how fandom is built and where new global businesses are emerging.”

Added Emma Lowe, director of the London Book Fair: “The London Book Fair is delighted to be working in partnership with the brilliant team at MIP Talks to meld together our fantastic worlds where stories are created, curated and sent out to find ever more fans, more audiences and more homes.”

articles.summary: Argonon, super-indie production group behind shows including “The Masked Singer U.K.,” has unveiled its biggest leadership changes since it was founded in 2011. Amanda Goddard, previously chief commercial and legal officer for Argonon, has been promoted to president and global CEO with a worldwide…
body: “Our sector is changing at breakneck pace; a restless state of constant evolution is the single most important mindset in a creative business,” said Burstall. “As platform agnostic storytellers whose content reaches millions of people across the world, we must be fearless, experimental, risk-taking and open to radical change to keep us at the cutting edge. Today’s announcement of a brand-new world class leadership team lays the foundations for an exciting future.”

The senior leadership team changes coincide with several new strategic initiatives across Argonon. The group is actively investing in digital and self-publishing content to build new IP and reach new audiences, exploring partnerships across the nations and regions, investing in its New York hubs, developing new high tech post facilities to support its London labels, and accelerating its AI capabilities. The group is also developing new innovative funding models to support IP creation and investment in content.

body: None of these queries are answered by the first seven episodes of “Wonka’s Golden Ticket,” but it’s still possible to puzzle out how we got here. articles.title: Matthew McConaughey and Woody Harrelson’s Comic Chemistry Isn’t Enough to Make ‘Brothers’ a Compelling Show: TV Review
articles.summary: “You have all the hallmarks of a world-class politician,” campaign manager Gwen (Lisa Gilroy) tells her client Matthew McConaughey (Matthew McConaughey). “However, your Achilles’ heel is that you’ve been a celebrity for so long that your brain has turned into a big old sloppy pile of goo.” The…
body: A reluctance to get messy or in any way unflattering is a common quality of star-driven shows, and it’s seemingly magnified when two of them are portraying themselves. “Brothers” prefers a soft poke to a sharp jab: Harrelson is a pot-smoking hippie who declines AC because he’s “off freon,” but when he makes a passing mention of COVID, it’s not to share his take on masking and vaccines; McConaughey quotes his own Lincoln commercials when giving his son a pep talk, but the greatest insecurity he’ll cop to is caring too much about being a good husband and father.
The first two episodes of “Brothers” will premiere on Apple TV on Sep. 23, with remaining episodes airing weekly on Wednesdays.

articles.title: Nigella Lawson is 'icing on the cake', TV critics say as she enters Bake Off tent
articles.summary: The TV chef joined Paul Hollywood in the tent as the Channel 4 competition returned for a new series.
body: TV critics have described Nigella Lawson as the "icing on the cake" of The Great British Bake Off, as the show returned for a new series on Tuesday.
Lawson has replaced Dame Prue Leith, who announced she was leaving earlier this year after nearly a decade in the programme's famous tent.
The Telegraph said Lawson gives the Channel 4 series a "new lease of life", while Digital Spy agreed she was a "brilliant addition" to the line-up.
But the Independent was cooler on the launch episode as a whole, saying the show "wastes Nigella's prodigious charms and misses chance for a true revamp".

articles.title: Prince and Princess of Wales share a laugh with Tom Cruise at film premiere
articles.summary: William and Catherine renew their friendship with the Hollywood star at the premiere for his film Digger.
body: The Prince and Princess of Wales renewed their friendship with Tom Cruise at the premiere of the Hollywood star's latest film in London on Tuesday.
Cruise took the hand of Catherine, Princess of Wales, as they talked and laughed on a black carpet - instead of the traditional red - before the royal gala screening of Digger in Leicester Square.
Cruise has known the prince and princess for a number of years and also met William's mother, Princess Diana, and attended her funeral in 1997.
Catherine wore a pair of Diana's pearl drop earrings to the premiere on Tuesday, as well as the late Queen Mother's amethyst sautoir necklace.

articles.title: ‘Brothers’ Review: Matthew McConaughey and Woody Harrelson Get Squandered in an Apple Sitcom That’s Barely Alright, Alright, Alright
articles.summary: The 'True Detective' co-stars reunite to play themselves in the eight-episode Texas-set comedy, which was run by David West Read ('Schitt's Creek') and then Lee Eisenberg ('WeCrashed').
body: For a sense of the decline in creative ambition between Matthew McConaughey and Woody Harrelson ‘s collaboration in HBO’s True Detective and Apple TV’s Brothers, one would have to imagine that after making Butch Cassidy and the Sundance Kid, Robert Redford and Paul Newman had made a movie that was primarily about how “Robert Redford” and “Paul Newman” loved to hang out and discuss how much fun it was to have made Butch Cassidy and the Sundance Kid.

Much as the Emmys recently asked the longtime friends to vamp for five or 10 minutes while presenting, in order to salvage an awards show with no particular direction, Brothers asks them to vamp for eight 30-minute episodes, in order to salvage a TV show with no particular direction.

It’s a tribute, then, to the charismatic energy generated by McConaughey and Harrelson’s partnership that no matter how hacky some of its sitcom tropes are, Brothers is generally, if never propulsively, engaging.

articles.title: 'Landing role on Thomas & Friends was crazy'
articles.summary: Ellie-Mae Siame, 14, says she was "in shock" but excited at being a part of the beloved series.
body: Earlier this year, young actor Ellie-Mae Siame landed a role in a show about one of the world's most recognisable characters – Thomas the Tank Engine.
The 14-year-old is the voice of Nia, the orange and black-coloured engine number 18 in Thomas & Friends: Railway Stories.
A full-length YouTube special premiered on Thursday, which has already been viewed more than two million times, and it will be on Netflix from 30 September before a full series airs in 2027.
"It was crazy to see how big Thomas the Tank Engine was – I knew it was big but not that big," Ellie-Mae told BBC Radio Stoke.
